participants.b: Parent and child authoritative name servers

intro.quote: To use DNSSEC RRs for authentication, a security-aware resolver requires configured knowledge of at least one authenticated DNSKEY or DS RR.

steps.explain: The resolver queries the parent zone for the DS RRset when the referral contains neither a DS RRset nor an NSEC RRset proving that no DS RRset exists.

cite.quote: A security-aware resolver MUST query the name servers for the parent zone for the DS RRset if the referral includes neither a DS RRset nor a NSEC RRset proving that the DS RRset does not exist (see Section 4).

steps.explain: When a DS RRset exists at the delegation point, the parent server returns it and its associated signatures in the Authority section with the NS RRset.

cite.quote: If a DS RRset is present at the delegation point, the name server MUST return both the DS RRset and its associated RRSIG RR(s) in the Authority section along with the NS RRset.

steps.explain: The resolver queries for the zone apex SOA or NS records with the DO bit set.

cite.quote: When responding to a query that has the DO bit set and that requests the SOA or NS RRs at the apex of a signed zone, a security-aware authoritative name server for that zone MAY return the zone apex DNSKEY RRset in the Additional section.

steps.explain: The child server may return the zone apex DNSKEY RRset in the Additional section so that the resolver can authenticate the delegation.

cite.quote: When responding to a query that has the DO bit set and that requests the SOA or NS RRs at the apex of a signed zone, a security-aware authoritative name server for that zone MAY return the zone apex DNSKEY RRset in the Additional section.

sequences.title: Proving that a name or type does not exist

intro.quote: A resolver can use authenticated NSEC RRs to prove that an RRset is not present in a signed zone.

steps.explain: The resolver may query for missing security records when the original response does not contain enough material to validate it.

cite.quote: Security-aware resolvers MAY query for missing security RRs in an attempt to perform validation; implementations that choose to do so must be aware that the answers received may not be sufficient to validate the original response.

steps.explain: For a name error, the server includes NSEC records and their associated signatures to prove that neither an exact name nor an applicable wildcard matches the request.

cite.quote:
If the zone does not contain any RRsets matching <SNAME, SCLASS> either exactly or via wildcard name expansion, then the name server MUST include the following NSEC RRs in the Authority section, along with their associated RRSIG RRs:

   o  An NSEC RR proving that there is no exact match for <SNAME,
      SCLASS>.

   o  An NSEC RR proving that the zone contains no RRsets that would
      match <SNAME, SCLASS> via wildcard name expansion.

steps.explain: If the response lacks the complete denial proof, the resolver resends the query to obtain the full collection of NSEC records.

cite.quote: If the complete set of necessary NSEC RRsets is not present in a response (perhaps due to message truncation), then a security-aware resolver MUST resend the query in order to attempt to obtain the full collection of NSEC RRs necessary to verify the non-existence of the requested RRset.

steps.explain: The renewed response supplies the NSEC proof records and their associated signatures.

cite.quote:
If the zone does not contain any RRsets matching <SNAME, SCLASS> either exactly or via wildcard name expansion, then the name server MUST include the following NSEC RRs in the Authority section, along with their associated RRSIG RRs:

   o  An NSEC RR proving that there is no exact match for <SNAME,
      SCLASS>.

   o  An NSEC RR proving that the zone contains no RRsets that would
      match <SNAME, SCLASS> via wildcard name expansion.

sequences.title: Handling a response whose signatures do not validate

intro.quote: If for whatever reason none of the RRSIGs can be validated, the response SHOULD be considered BAD.

steps.explain: The client sends a recursive query so that the recursive name server performs validation.

cite.quote: If for whatever reason none of the RRSIGs can be validated, the response SHOULD be considered BAD. If the validation was being done to service a recursive query, the name server MUST return RCODE 2 to the originating client. However, it MUST return the full response if and only if the original query had the CD bit set.

steps.explain: When no signature validates for a recursive query, the recursive name server returns server failure. It returns the full response only when the original query had the CD bit set.
